mainTopic: Does טבילה (and שחיטה) need כוונה? The wave and water-channel sources, רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן בן יוסף, and רבי נתן versus the רבנן.
overview: The גמרא keeps asking whether טבילה needs כוונה. First it shows that the משנה about a breaking wave proves nothing, and it explains what that משנה teaches: we make no גזירה against a wave, though one may not immerse in its arcs up in the air. Next it proves from the משנה about fruit in a water channel that טבילה for חולין works without כוונה. רבא challenges רב נחמן twice from the wording of another משנה, and then a ברייתא openly backs רב נחמן. אביי asks whether this refutes רבי יוחנן, and רב יוסף answers that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יונתן בן יוסף, who learns from the צרעת garment that immersion needs intent. רב שימי בר אשי objects from the סתם משנה about a dropped knife, and the גמרא answers that שחיטה of חולין is an exception that even רבי יונתן בן יוסף accepts. Along the way it explains the מחלוקת of רבי נתן and the רבנן about intent to cut. רב פפא then describes the forced-נדה case according to each view. The amud ends with רבא's ruling that a פרה אדומה slaughtered together with another animal is פסולה according to everyone.

steps.title: Flipping the comparison: vessels are like a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof that no כוונה is needed by reversing the comparison. Vessels are compared to the person, so they also need a person's intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And vessels are like a person. Just as a person needs intent, so too vessels need a person to have intent for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on an earlier proof. That proof said the person in the משנה is like the vessels, so no כוונה is needed. The גמרא says you can read it the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof was: vessels need no intent, so the person in the same משנה needs none either. The גמרא answers that the comparison works just as well in reverse. A person needs כוונה, so the vessels are purified only when a person intends to purify them. Since both readings are possible, the משנה proves nothing about whether כוונה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to, compared with
intent, specifically the intent to purify through immersion
vessels, utensils
has intent, intends

steps.confusionAlert: Vessels have no mind of their own. When the גמרא says vessels need כוונה, it means the person who owns or handles them must intend that they become pure.

phrases.english: And vessels are similar to a person:
just as for a person we require intent,
so too vessels as well
are purified where a person intends for them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵלִים דּוּמְיָא דְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier inference from the משנה that no כוונה is needed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the נחשול משנה that immersion needs no כוונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison between the person and the vessels can be read in either direction, so it does not decide anything.

steps.title: If he sits and waits, what is new?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is talking about someone who sits and waits for the wave with intent, the ruling seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה is about someone who sits and waits for the wave, what is it telling us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just suggested. If the person is sitting and waiting for the wave on purpose, the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the משנה as needing כוונה means the person intended the immersion. A wave holding forty סאה with full intent sounds like an ordinary valid immersion. So the גמרא asks what new point the משנה is making.

keyTerms.meaning: sits and waits, watching for the wave with intent
what is the point of saying it? It seems obvious

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is about one who sits and waits,
phrases.notes: He is waiting for the moment the wave breaks off so that he can immerse in it.

phrases.english: what is the point of stating it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בְּיוֹשֵׁב וּמְצַפֶּה מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading proposed in step 1 by asking what the משנה would add.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as a case of יושב ומצפה, meaning with כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With intent and forty סאה, purity is obvious, so a משנה should not be needed to teach it.

steps.title: The novelty: no decree is made
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that we do not forbid the wave because of rain cascades, and we do not forbid its edges because of its arcs.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should make a decree because of a cascade of rainwater. Or we should forbid the edges of the wave because of its arcs. The משנה teaches us that we do not make these decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The new point of the משנה is that the חכמים did not make two possible גזירות against immersing in a wave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First worry: people might confuse a wave with a חרדלית של גשמים, flowing rainwater that cannot purify. Second worry: if we allow the edges of the wave, which touch the ground, people might also immerse in the arcs, which are up in the air. The משנה tells us that neither worry led to a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have thought (this introduces the mistaken idea the source rules out)
let us make a rabbinic decree
a cascade of flowing rainwater, which does not purify
the edges of the wave that touch the ground
the arcs of the wave, curved up in the air
it teaches us (the actual new point)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the נחשול can be read as needing כוונה. Its new point is that we do not decree against a wave, either because of rain cascades or because of its arcs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a משנה can stay meaningful even when its case looks simple, because it rules out a גזירה you might have expected.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
let us decree because of a cascade of rainwater,
phrases.notes: The worry is that people would think flowing rainwater purifies too. It does not.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי לִיגְזַר רָאשִׁין אַטּוּ כִּיפִּין,
phrases.english: alternatively, let us decree against the edges because of the arcs,
it teaches us that we do not decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לִיגְזַר מִשּׁוּם חַרְדָּלִית שֶׁל גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is new' challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden novelty: ruling out a possible גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have decreed against wave immersion because of rain cascades, or against the edges because of the arcs.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such decrees were made. Immersion in a wave with forty סאה works.

steps.title: Source for not immersing in the arcs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that immersion in the arc of a wave is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say that we do not immerse in the arcs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for something it just assumed: that the arcs of a wave are not valid for immersion. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second possible decree only makes sense if immersing in the arcs is invalid. The גמרא wants to see where that rule is written before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
we immerse (something to purify it)

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we do not immerse in the arcs?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּלָא מַטְבְּלִינַן בְּכִיפִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption behind the second decree in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that immersion in the arcs of a wave is invalid.

steps.title: A taught source: no immersion in the air
steps.stepSummary: A taught source says one may immerse in the edges of a wave but not in its arcs, because one may not immerse in the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one may immerse in the edges, but not in the arcs, because one may not immerse in the air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a taught source. It states plainly that the arcs are invalid because water in the air does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The edges of the wave rest on the ground, so they work like a proper gathering of water. The arcs hang in the air, and immersion must be in water that rests on the ground. This confirms the rule that step 3 relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: one may immerse
air; water that is up in the air and not resting on the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Immersion has to be in water resting on the ground. The edges of a wave are fine, but its airborne arcs are not.

phrases.english: As we learned: one may immerse in the edges,
but one may not immerse in the arcs,
because one may not immerse in the air.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן מַטְבִּילִין בְּרָאשִׁין וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בְּכִיפִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the arcs of a wave are invalid for immersion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A taught source: מטבילין בראשין ואין מטבילין בכיפין שאין מטבילין באויר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Immersion must take place in water resting on the ground, never in airborne water.

steps.title: What is the source that non-sacred food needs no intent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again for a source showing that immersion for חולין works without כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in any case, where do we learn that non-sacred items do not need intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier proof was pushed away, so the גמרא asks again for a real source that חולין needs no כוונה. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the wave was rejected because vessels were compared to the person. The idea that חולין needs no כוונה still stands, but it now needs its own source. The word אלא shows we are dropping the old proof and searching for a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular, non-sacred food (not קדשים or תרומה)
In any case, at least
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: But non-sacred items, which do not require intent
in any case, from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חוּלִּין דְּלָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּונָה מִיהָא מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wave proof was rejected in Step 1 and its משנה explained in Steps 2-5, the גמרא returns to look for a new source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that immersion for חולין is valid without כוונה.

steps.title: Proof from produce that fell into a water channel
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that someone who reached into a stream to take fruit has pure hands even without intending to immerse them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If fruit fell into a water channel, and someone with impure hands reached in and took it, his hands are pure, and the fruit is not in the category of 'when water is placed.' But if he put his hands in so they would be rinsed, his hands are pure, and the fruit is in the category of 'when water is placed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as its answer. A man with impure hands grabbed fruit out of a stream without meaning to immerse his hands, and still his hands became pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case he only wanted the fruit, yet the משנה says his hands are pure. That shows purity for חולין comes even without כוונה to immerse. The second case adds a difference: when he wanted his hands wet, the water counts as wanted, so the fruit can now become impure (כי יותן).

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel or stream
Hands that are ritually impure
'When water is placed': the rule that food can become impure only after it gets wet with the owner's approval
So that they will be rinsed

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here. The hands become pure in both cases. The only difference between the cases is whether the fruit becomes able to receive impurity (כי יותן), and that depends on whether he wanted the water.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Produce that fell into a water channel
and someone whose hands were impure reached out
and took them: his hands are pure
and the produce is not in the category of "when water is placed."
But if he did it so that his hands would be rinsed,
they are pure, and the produce is in the category of "when water is placed."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: פֵּירוֹת שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ אַמַּת הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That immersion for חולין works without כוונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about fruit in a water channel: the hands are pure even when he only reached in to take the fruit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the main source that חולין needs no כוונה, and the next steps test that view.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the wording 'assumed status'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה whose wording seems to say that even for חולין, a person must have in mind to become pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן: If someone immersed for non-sacred food and took on the status of purity for non-sacred food, he is forbidden to eat מעשר. This suggests: if he took on that status, yes, he may eat non-sacred food; if he did not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן, who holds that חולין needs no כוונה. He reads a משנה closely to show that intent seems to be needed even for חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'he immersed for חולין and assumed status for חולין.' רבא reads it this way: only if he deliberately took on the purity status does he become pure for חולין, and without that he does not. That would mean כוונה matters even for חולין, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed
He took on, or was given, the status (here, of purity)
Tithe produce (here, מעשר שני), which needs a higher level of purity than חולין
Yes

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
If one immersed for non-sacred food and took on purity status for non-sacred food,
he is forbidden to eat tithe.
If he took on that status, yes, he may eat non-sacred food;
if he did not take it on, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position just supported in Step 7 that חולין needs no כוונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that immersion for חולין needs no כוונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from the wording 'והוחזק לחולין' suggests that without deliberately taking on purity status, one is not pure even for חולין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the משנה means 'even though'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the משנה as 'even though he became pure for חולין, he is still forbidden in מעשר,' so it does not require intent for חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: Even though he has taken on purity status for non-sacred food, he is forbidden to eat tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא by reading the משנה's wording differently. The 'assumed status' part is not a condition for חולין; it is a lead-in to the ruling about מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read 'הוחזק' as a requirement: only with it is he pure for חולין. רב נחמן reads it as 'even though': he is already pure for חולין, and still he may not eat מעשר. So the משנה is only teaching about מעשר and says nothing about needing כוונה for חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, a rereading of a source
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's view stands: immersion for חולין works without כוונה, as the water-channel משנה shows. The 'assumed status' משנה means 'even though he is pure for חולין, he still cannot eat מעשר.'

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Even though he took on purity status for non-sacred food,
he is forbidden to eat tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּחְזַק לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in Step 8 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source ('and he assumed' becomes 'even though he assumed').
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'והוחזק לחולין' is a condition, so without deliberately taking on purity status he is not pure even for חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is a concession: he is already pure for חולין, and the משנה teaches only that he is still forbidden in מעשר.

steps.title: רבא challenges again from the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes 'he immersed and did not take on the status, it is as if he did not immerse' and argues it means the immersion did nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן: 'If someone immersed but did not mean to become pure, it is as if he did not immerse.' Doesn't that mean it is as if he did not immerse at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן again, using another line of the same משנה. This line sounds like an immersion without intent counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן just said intent is only needed for מעשר, not for חולין. רבא points to the words 'as if he did not immerse.' Read plainly, they sound total: the immersion did not help even for חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed (in a מקוה or spring)
Took on the status (here, meant to become pure)
Doesn't it mean...? (a challenging reading)
At all

phrases.english: He objected to him: If he immersed but did not take on the status of purity –
phrases.notes: רבא is objecting to רב נחמן. 'Did not take on the status' means he didn't have in mind to become pure.

phrases.english: it is as though he did not immerse.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: כְּאִילּוּ לֹא טָבַל כְּלָל?
phrases.english: Doesn't it mean: as though he did not immerse at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: טָבַל וְלֹא הוּחְזַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge from the same משנה after רב נחמן answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's position that immersion for חולין needs no intent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'As though he did not immerse' sounds total, so the immersion fails even for חולין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: not immersed for מעשר, but immersed for חולין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the phrase. It is as if he did not immerse only for מעשר. For חולין the immersion worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it is as if he did not immerse for מעשר, but he did immerse for חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא the same way as before. The line only talks about מעשר, not about חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads 'as though he did not immerse' as limited. It means 'did not immerse for the higher level of מעשר.' So the משנה still fits his view that חולין needs no intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe (מעשר שני), which needs a higher level of purity
Ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: No, it is as though he did not immerse for tithe,
but he did immerse for non-sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, כְּאִילּוּ לֹא טָבַל לְמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's words (only for מעשר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The immersion counts for nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It fails only for מעשר. For חולין it works without intent.

steps.title: רבא finds a ברייתא that backs רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רבא thought רב נחמן was just brushing him off. Then he looked and found a ברייתא saying exactly what רב נחמן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא thought רב נחמן was just pushing him away. He went out, checked, and found a ברייתא: 'If he immersed and did not mean to become pure, he is permitted for חולין and forbidden for מעשר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב נחמן's reading was not just a quick escape. A ברייתא openly says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב נחמן's readings could have looked like forced answers. The ברייתא states the rule directly: without intent, he is pure for חולין but not for מעשר. This gives solid proof that חולין needs no intent.

keyTerms.meaning: He is just pushing him off (giving a weak answer to get rid of him)
He went out, looked carefully, and found
Permitted
Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer to our question: immersion without intent works for חולין but not for מעשר. A ברייתא says so openly.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סָבַר: דַּיחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He thought: he is just pushing him off.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא, who thought רב נחמן's answers were not the real meaning.

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found,
as it is taught: If he immersed and did not take on the status of purity –
he is permitted for non-sacred food
and forbidden for tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא סָבַר: דַּיחוֹיֵי קָא מְדַחֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that רב נחמן's answers in steps 9 and 11 were correct.
steps.raayaObject: Immersion for חולין works without intent, but not for מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: טבל ולא הוחזק מותר לחולין ואסור למעשר

steps.title: אביי asks if this ברייתא refutes רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether this ברייתא disproves רבי יוחנן, who required intent even for a matter of חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Should we say this ברייתא is a refutation of רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now uses the ברייתא against רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said earlier that a נדה who immersed without intent is still forbidden to her husband. Her husband is a matter of חולין, not holy food. But the ברייתא says intent is not needed for חולין, so it seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (suggesting a conclusion)
A refutation that knocks out an opinion
From this (source)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Shall we say there is a refutation
of Rabbi Yochanan from this?
phrases.notes: Earlier on the דף, רבי יוחנן said a נדה who immersed without intent stays forbidden to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 12 to challenge an earlier ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a נדה who immersed without intent is forbidden to her husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says immersion for חולין needs no intent. A wife returning to her husband is a matter of חולין, so the immersion should work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יונתן בן יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רבי יוחנן holds like another תנא, רבי יונתן בן יוסף, who requires intent. So the ברייתא does not bind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוחנן says his ruling following רבי יונתן בן יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רבי יוחנן. He has a תנא on his side, so one ברייתא going the other way does not refute him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא can be refuted by a ברייתא only if no תנא agrees with him. Here רבי יוחנן follows רבי יונתן בן יוסף, who holds that intent is needed. So this is a disagreement among תנאים, not a refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: He is the one who rules following (another sage)
Intent, having in mind

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not refute רבי יוחנן. He sides with רבי יונתן בן יוסף, a תנא who requires intent.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yochanan is saying his view
in accordance with Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the אמורא follows a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יונתן בן יוסף, who requires intent, so he is not refuted.

steps.title: The source: רבי יונתן בן יוסף requires intent for the second washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יונתן בן יוסף requires intent. From the extra word 'שנית' he compares the second washing (immersion) to the first washing, which is done with intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: The verse could have said just 'and it shall be washed.' Why does it add 'a second time'? It compares the second washing to the first washing. Just as the first washing is done with intent, so too the second washing must be done with intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing where רב יוסף got his claim that a תנא, רבי יונתן בן יוסף, requires intent for immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of a garment with צרעת, the first washing happens because the כהן commands it, so it is clearly done with intent. The extra word 'שנית' links the second washing, the immersion, to the first one. So the immersion also needs intent, even though the garment is not קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this? (pointing to an extra word)
Compares two things in the verse so they share the same rule (a היקש)
A washing; here, first the laundering and then the immersion
With intent, on purpose

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says:
"And it shall be washed": why does the verse say "a second time"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:58, about a garment with צרעת.

phrases.english: It compares the second washing to the first washing:
just as the first washing is done with intent,
so too the second washing is done with intent.
phrases.notes: The 'second washing' is the immersion in a מקוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב יוסף's claim in step 14 that רבי יונתן בן יוסף requires intent.
steps.raayaObject: That a תנא exists who requires intent even for immersion of something that is not קודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף on ויקרא 13:58 ('וכובס שנית').

steps.title: Should the immersion also need a כהן's intent?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, a challenge comes up. If the comparison is complete, then just as the first washing needs a כהן's command, the immersion should also need a כהן's intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you might say: just as there, by the first washing, we need the intent of a כהן, so too here, by the second washing, we should need the intent of a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests how far the comparison goes. Maybe it carries over every detail, including the need for a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש might copy all the features of one case onto the other. The first washing was done by the command of a כהן. So the question is whether the immersion also needs a כהן's intent, and not just anyone's intent.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as there… (pushing a comparison further)
The intent or command of a כהן

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן בָּעֵינַן דַּעַת כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: If so: just as there we require the intent of a priest,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the first washing, which the כהן orders (ויקרא 13:54).

phrases.english: so too here should we require the intent of a priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן בָּעֵינַן דַּעַת כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison in step 15 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The היקש between the first and second washing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, the immersion should also need a כהן's intent, just like the first washing.

steps.title: 'וטהר' teaches that any person's intent is enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the word 'וטהר' (and it shall be pure). The garment becomes pure in any case, without a כהן. Ordinary intent is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'and it shall be pure,' which means in any case, even without a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits the comparison. Intent is needed, but it does not have to be a כהן's intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וטהר' shows that purity comes no matter who does the immersion. So the היקש carries over only the need for intent, not the need for a כהן. The final result is that רבי יונתן בן יוסף requires intent for this immersion of something that is not קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be pure (ויקרא 13:58)
In any case, no matter what

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונתן בן יוסף: immersion needs intent (from 'שנית') but not a כהן's intent (from 'וטהר'). This is the view רב יוסף says רבי יוחנן follows.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And it shall be pure", in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְטָהֵר״, מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second word in the verse limits the היקש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The immersion needs a כהן's intent, like the first washing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any person's intent is enough; no כהן is needed.

steps.title: Would רבי יוחנן really require intent?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי questions whether רבי יוחנן really holds that intent is needed. רבי יוחנן himself rules that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי challenged this: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows an unnamed משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: A new attack begins on רב יוסף's answer. This line sets up the challenge, and the next step brings the משנה that makes it work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general rule: when a משנה is stated without a name, the הלכה follows it. If some סתם משנה holds that intent is not needed, רבי יוחנן should rule that way. Then he could not be following רבי יונתן בן יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it (a strong objection)
Did he really say this?
The הלכה follows a משנה stated with no name attached

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi challenged it:
And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's link (step 14) between רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן בן יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יונתן בן יוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own rule makes him follow a סתם משנה. If a סתם משנה does not require intent, he cannot be following רבי יונתן בן יוסף.

steps.title: The סתם משנה: a dropped knife is valid without intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the סתם משנה about a knife that fell and slaughtered. From it we learn that if a person dropped the knife, the slaughter is valid without intent. רבא says this is רבי נתן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: If a knife fell and slaughtered an animal, the slaughter is invalid, even though it cut in the normal way. And we discussed this: The reason is that it fell by itself. But if he dropped it, the slaughter is valid, even though he did not intend to slaughter. And we asked: Which תנא holds that slaughter does not need intent? רבא said: It is רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב שימי בר אשי's attack. It shows a סתם משנה, following רבי נתן, that does not require intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only rules out a knife that fell on its own. So a person who dropped it, even without meaning to slaughter, makes a valid שחיטה. This סתם משנה matches רבי נתן, who does not require intent. By רבי יוחנן's rule, he should follow רבי נתן and not רבי יונתן בן יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: The knife fell by itself
He dropped it (a human act)
In its normal way (a proper cut)
Intent to slaughter
Invalid / valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'fell' (נפלה, no person acted) with 'dropped' (הפילה, a person acted without meaning to slaughter). Only the first one is invalid. The proof comes from the second one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real conflict: רבי יוחנן's rule about סתם משנה seems to put him on the side of not requiring intent.

phrases.english: And we learned: If a knife fell and slaughtered,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁחֲטָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ – פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: even though it slaughtered in the normal way, it is invalid.
And we discussed it:
The reason is that it fell,
but if he dropped it, it is valid,
even though he did not intend.
And we said: Who is the tanna
who does not require intent for slaughter?
Rava said: It is Rabbi Natan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: נָפְלָה סַכִּין וְשָׁחֲטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the סתם משנה that completes the challenge begun in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That a סתם משנה, following רבי נתן, does not require intent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of נפלה סכין ושחטה, with the inference about הפילה and רבא's naming of רבי נתן.

steps.title: Slaughter is different: even the strict view agrees no intent is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שחיטה is a special case. Even רבי יונתן בן יוסף agrees that שחיטה of חולין needs no intent, because the תורה required intent only for קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to slaughter, even רבי יונתן בן יוסף agrees that intent is not needed. The תורה showed that a קרבן slaughtered without intent is invalid, which means that for ordinary animals we do not need intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב שימי בר אשי's question. רבי יוחנן can require intent for immersion and still accept the סתם משנה about the knife, because שחיטה is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה had to teach that a מתעסק, someone acting without intent, is פסול by קדשים. If intent were always needed, that teaching would add nothing. So by implication, חולין do not need intent, and רבי יוחנן's two positions do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees, admits
someone who does an act without meaning to do it
sacrificial animals
ordinary, non-sacred animals
by implication, from the general sense
intent

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יונתן בן יוסף changed his mind about immersion. He still needs intent for טבילה. He only agrees that שחיטה of חולין is an exception.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁחִיטָה, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף [מוֹדֵי],
phrases.english: With regard to slaughter, even Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef [agrees],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Even רבי יונתן בן יוסף agrees that for slaughter, intent isn't needed.

phrases.english: since the Merciful One revealed
that one who acts without intent with sacrifices is invalid —
which implies that for non-sacred animals we do not require intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁחִיטָה, אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף מוֹדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of רב שימי בר אשי, which was built on the סתם משנה of the knife.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: שחיטה is set apart from טבילה by a תורה source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יוחנן requires intent for immersion, he should require it for שחיטה too, and that would clash with the סתם משנה he follows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה limited the intent requirement for שחיטה to קדשים, so חולין need no intent even according to רבי יונתן בן יוסף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יוחנן can rule like the סתם משנה about the knife and still hold that immersion needs intent.

steps.title: The Rabbis' view: no intent to slaughter, but intent to cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the view of the רבנן who argue with רבי נתן. They agree no intent is needed to slaughter, but they hold that a person must at least intend to cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן would say: granted that we do not need intent to slaughter, we do need intent to cut.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just said חולין need no intent, it now explains what the רבנן, who invalidate a thrown knife, must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן split the act into two kinds of intent. Intent to perform a שחיטה is not required. Intent to make a cutting motion is required, so a knife that was thrown down and happened to cut is not good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, even if
slaughtering, meaning the act as a שחיטה
cutting, the physical act of cutting

phrases.english: And the Rabbis [would say]:
granted that we do not require intent for slaughtering,
for cutting we do require it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, נְהִי דְּלָא בָּעֵינַן כַּוָּונָה לִזְבִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that חולין need no intent, it explains how the רבנן can still invalidate the thrown knife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, שחיטה of חולין does not need intent to slaughter, but it does need intent to cut.

steps.title: רבא: the verse says 'slaughter', not 'cut'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי נתן defeated the רבנן with this argument. The תורה says 'וזבחת', not 'וחתכת', so cutting and slaughtering cannot be treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: with this argument רבי נתן beat the רבנן. Does the verse say 'and you shall cut'? It says 'and you shall slaughter'. If we need intent for cutting, we should need it for slaughtering too. If we do not need intent for slaughtering, we should not need it for cutting either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the רבנן's split between slaughtering and cutting, and he presents this as רבי נתן's winning argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses only one word, 'וזבחת'. Nothing in it gives cutting a separate intent requirement. So both kinds of intent stand or fall together, and since slaughtering needs no intent, cutting needs none either.

keyTerms.meaning: he defeated them, won the argument against them
is it written? (a challenge from the wording of the verse)
it should be required

steps.whatToRemember: Following רבי נתן and רבא, שחיטה of חולין needs no intent at all, not even intent to cut. That is why a dropped knife that slaughters properly is kosher.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זְכָנְהוּ רַבִּי נָתָן לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rava said: With this Rabbi Natan defeated the Rabbis:
Is it written "and you shall cut"?
"And you shall slaughter" is written,
if we require intent for cutting —
we should require it even for slaughtering;
if we do not require intent for slaughtering —
we should not require it for cutting either.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּהָא זְכָנְהוּ רַבִּי נָתָן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's distinction that was presented in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The רבנן's split between intent to slaughter and intent to cut.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse says only 'וזבחת'. It gives no separate source for an intent to cut, so the two cannot be treated differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the side discussion and confirms רבי נתן's view that a dropped knife can slaughter properly.

steps.title: What exactly is the case of a forced נדה immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the case of a נדה who immersed against her will and asks what the situation actually looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances of a נדה who was forced and immersed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic of immersion without intent. It asks for the exact case, setting up the possible answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To know whether this case shows immersion working without intent, we first need to know who did the forcing. Different setups give different answers about whether any intent was present.

keyTerms.meaning: what are the circumstances? what case is this?
a woman who is ritually impure from her monthly period
she was forced, against her will
immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a menstruating woman who was forced and immersed?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי נִדָּה שֶׁנֶּאֶנְסָה וְטָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שחיטה side topic and goes back to the earlier discussion of immersion without intent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case of a forced immersion, and specifically who forced her.

steps.title: If her friend forced her, there is real intent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that another woman forced her into the water, then rejects that idea, because the other woman's intent counts as full intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say her friend forced her and immersed her, then the friend's intent is real, full intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first way to picture the case and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another woman deliberately immersed her, someone did have intent, and that intent counts fully. Then the immersion should work even for רבי יוחנן, who requires intent, so this cannot be the case under discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say, a proposed explanation that is about to be rejected
proper, full intent

phrases.english: If we say that her friend forced her and immersed her,
the intent of her friend is full-fledged intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא דְּאַנְסַהּ חֲבִירְתַּהּ וְאַטְבְּלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 23 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the forced immersion was carried out by another woman.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The other woman's intent is full intent, so the case would not be immersion without intent at all.

steps.title: A second reason the other-woman case cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second reason to reject the idea that another woman pushed her in. If that counted, she would even be allowed to eat תרומה, as the משנה about women who cannot prepare themselves shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, in that case she would even be allowed to eat תרומה. We learned: a deaf-mute woman, a שוטה, a blind woman, or a woman who lost her mind may eat תרומה if competent women prepare them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more reason why the forced immersion cannot mean another woman put her in the water. It brings a משנה to show that such an immersion is fully valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling treated the forced immersion as weaker, good for her husband but apparently not for תרומה. But the משנה says a woman who cannot prepare herself may eat תרומה when a competent woman prepares her. So an immersion done by another woman counts completely, and it cannot be the weaker case we are looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which may only be eaten in a state of full purity
A deaf-mute woman, treated as lacking full understanding
A woman who is mentally incompetent
Competent, clear-minded women
They prepare them, meaning they check them and immerse them

phrases.english: And furthermore, she would even be able to eat תרומה,
as we learned: the deaf-mute woman, and the mentally incompetent woman,
and the blind woman, and the one whose mind became unsettled,
if they have competent women
who prepare them, they may eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, בִּתְרוּמָה נָמֵי אָכְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason supporting the rejection in step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that the forced immersion means another woman put her into the water
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An immersion done by another woman counts fully, even for תרומה, so it cannot be the weaker forced-immersion case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a חרשת, שוטה, סומא and one who lost her mind, who may eat תרומה when competent women prepare them

steps.title: רב פפא explains the forced-immersion case for each view
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the question from step 23. For רבי נתן, who needs no intent at all, she fell off a bridge into the water. For the רבנן, who need at least an intent to do the action, she went into the water to cool off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: According to רבי נתן, she fell off a bridge. According to the רבנן, she went down into the water to cool off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finally answers what 'immersed against her will' looks like. He gives a different case for each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן said no intent is needed, so even falling into the water with no thought at all works. The רבנן need her at least to mean to enter the water, like intending to cut in שחיטה. So for them the case is going in to cool off, which is on purpose but not for purity.

keyTerms.meaning: A bridge
To cool off
She fell, meaning it happened with no intent at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן: no intent needed at all, so even falling in counts. רבנן: she must at least mean to do the act, like going in to cool off, even without thinking about purity.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: According to Rabbi Natan,
it is where she fell off the bridge,
and according to the Rabbis, it is where she went down to cool off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְרַבִּי נָתָן, שֶׁנָּפְלָה מִן הַגֶּשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer to the question of step 23, after steps 24 and 25 rejected the other-woman case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the case of a נדה who immersed against her will
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי נתן, she fell from a bridge. For the רבנן, she went into the water to cool off.

steps.title: Slaughtering a red heifer together with another animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new case. If someone slaughtered a פרה אדומה and in the same cut slaughtered another animal with it, everyone agrees the פרה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone slaughtered a פרה and slaughtered another animal together with it, everyone agrees it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new case connected to the מחלוקת of רבי נתן and the רבנן about intent. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'According to everyone' means that here both רבי נתן and the רבנן agree. Whatever their argument about intent, slaughtering the פרה אדומה together with another animal disqualifies it. The גמרא will now go on to discuss this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify people from טומאת מת
According to everyone, meaning all sides of the מחלוקת agree
Disqualified, here meaning the פרה is invalid for its purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this case belongs only to one side. 'לדברי הכל' means even רבי נתן, who is lenient about intent, agrees the פרה is פסולה here.

phrases.english: Rava said: If one slaughtered a heifer
phrases.notes: This is the red heifer, the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: and slaughtered another animal along with it,
according to everyone, it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שָׁחַט פָּרָה וְשָׁחַט בְּהֵמָה אַחֶרֶת עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the forced-immersion case to a new case tied to the מחלוקת of רבי נתן and the רבנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering a פרה אדומה together with another animal disqualifies the פרה, and all sides agree
